text:
Utah has a rival now. Gabriel Landeskog was fined for cross-checking Logan Cooley, Jack McBain answered by fighting Landeskog, and the Mammoth's Liam O'Brien put it plainly in the Denver Post: "If you touch any of our top guys, me and the boys are coming for you." The two teams just unveiled their uniforms for the Winter Classic, where they meet.

On the ice, the Mammoth control play and haven't fully been paid for it. They have 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 57% at 5v5, but they're 12-9-3, and by our numbers they've earned about three more points than they have. The gap is mostly in net: Utah has allowed about nine more goals than its chances against would predict. The last ten games went 3-4-3 on 53% of the expected goals, which looks like a better team than the record.

Our playoff odds still have Utah at 72%. Cooley is the engine, with 14 points in his last 10 games on 10.5 expected, a hot run backed by real chances. The quiet force is the Anders Lee, Kailer Yamamoto and Barrett Hayton line, which wins 72% of the expected goals at 5v5.

The worry is the top pair. MacKenzie Weegar and Mikhail Sergachev win 56% of the expected goals but have been on for 6 goals for and 14 against at 5v5. It is the clearest spot where better saves would change the season.
